Here, a great blue heron perches over the west branch of the DuPage River.</p></figcaption><span class="line"></span><div class="Figure-credit"><p>Pat Nabong/Sun-Times</p></div></div> </figure> </div> </div><p></p><h4><a class="Link" href="https://paddleillinoiswatertrails.org/projects/upper-little-calumet-river/" target="_blank" ><b><u>Little Calumet River</u></b></a></h4><p><b>Where:</b> In southern Cook near Riverdale</p><p><b>What to know:</b> A paddle in this small, calm stream from Gouwens Park in South Holland to the Little Calumet Boat Launch in Blue Island is seven miles; get out after five miles at Kickapoo Woods. A trip on the deeper dredged section of the Calumet River begins at the newly refurbished dock at Beaubien Woods near the historic Altgeld Gardens housing development.</p><h4>﻿<a class="Link" href="https://paddleillinoiswatertrails.org/water-trails/trails-by-waterway/salt-creek-water-trails/" target="_blank" ><b><u>Salt Creek</u></b></a></h4><p><b>Where:</b> Drive west 45 minutes toward Westchester</p><p><b>What to know:</b> Salt Creek winds through Cook County forest preserves. A good start is a six-mile trip from Bemis Woods to a nice improved landing at Brookfield Village Hall; it’s another mile to Plank Road where the creek empties into the Des Plaines. More experienced paddlers can continue another two miles on the Des Plaines to Stony Ford landing, which will take you through a mild Class 1 stretch of waves in Riverside where the old Hofmann Dam once stood. Find details at Openlands.</p><h3><b>Moving water trips: Northern Illinois</b></h3><p><i>Looking to venture a little further? Northern Illinois offers some beautiful rivers and creeks in natural settings. Details for most rivers can be found at the </i><a class="Link" href="https://openlands.org/" target="_blank" ><i><u>Openlands website.</u></i></a></p><h4><a class="Link" href="https://paddleillinoiswatertrails.org/water-trails/trails-by-waterway/kishwaukee/" target="_blank" ><b><u>Kishwaukee River</u></b></a></h4><p><b>Where:</b> Head northwest to Belvidere</p><p><b>What to know:</b> The medium-sized “Kish” is one of the most scenic and pleasant rivers in Illinois, well-tended by its many local devotees. A six-mile family friendly trip is Espenscheid Memorial Forest Preserve to Atwood Park.</p><p><a class="Link" href="https://rocktownadventures.com/" target="_blank" ><u>Rocktown Adventures</u></a> in Rockford is a respected resource for lessons and gear, and provides rentals for the Kishwaukee and the Rock, which is right on site.</p><h4><a class="Link" href="https://paddleillinoiswatertrails.org/water-trails/trails-by-waterway/fox-river-water-trails/" target="_blank" ><b><u>Fox River</u></b></a><b>, </b><a class="Link" href="https://rockrivertrail.com/water-trail/" target="_blank" ><b><u>Rock River</u></b></a> and <a class="Link" href="https://openlands.org/waterway/kankakee-river-trails/" target="_blank" ><b><u>Kankakee River</u></b></a></h4><p><b>Where:</b> The Fox at Yorkville is about one hour drive from Chicago; the Rock is further west another hour to Castle Rock State Park near Oregon. And the Kankakee River ends where it flows into the Des Plaines near Channahon, forming the Illinois River.</p><p><b>What to know:</b> The three rivers are on the larger side and usually have enough water to paddle year around. The Fox and Rock have a “dells” section with deep canyons and high sandstone cliffs. Groups that offer lessons and rentals on the Fox are <a class="Link" href="https://www.howlingwolfe.com/" target="_blank" ><u>Howling Wolfe</u></a> in Aurora, and <a class="Link" href="https://yakshackonline.com/" target="_blank" ><u>The Yak Shack</u></a> in Yorkville, where there is also a short Class 1-2 whitewater course.</p><h4><a class="Link" href="https://paddleillinoiswatertrails.org/water-trails/trails-by-waterway/nippersink/" target="_blank" ><b><u>Nippersink Creek</u></b></a></h4><p>Where: Drive north toward McHenry County</p><p><b>What to know: </b>This is a narrow, curving creek that cuts through the nature-rich Glacial Park Conservation Area and the Hackmatack National Wildlife Refuge. The water quality is very high, in part a result of the county’s stream restoration project to re-meander a straightened agricultural ditch. The most popular <a class="Link" href="https://www.mccdistrict.org/visit___explore/things_to_do/paddle.php" target="_blank" ><u>trip</u></a> is seven miles from Keystone Landing to Pioneer Landing.</p>

entries.title: Vehicle fatally crashes into pedestrian changing tire during I-80 hit-and-run in Lansing
entries.summary: <p>State police are urging anyone who captured dashcam video or has information about a deadly crash early Wednesday on I-80 that left a pedestrian changing their tire dead in south suburban Lansing to contact them. </p><p>Troopers were called at about 5:28 a.m. to westbound I-80 at Torrence Avenue for a report of a pedestrian being struck, police said. The vehicle then left the scene. </p><p>The pedestrian, who had been trying to change a tire on their vehicle when they were hit, was dead at the scene, according to state police. Their identity, age and gender have not been released. </p><p>Two lanes of traffic remained closed as of 8 a.m. and police are asking that anyone with information or dashcam video call Illinois State Police Zone 1 at <a class="Link" href="tel:8472944400" target="_blank" >847-294-4400</a> or email <a class="Link" href="mailto:ISP.CrimeTips@Illinois.gov" target="_blank" >ISP.CrimeTips@Illinois.gov</a>. Police said witnesses can remain anonymous.<br></p>

Kang</a></h5><p><b>Chicago vs. Airbnb</b>: The city has filed a lawsuit accusing short-term rental company Airbnb and one of its hosts of improperly listing numerous properties.</p><p><b>What's alleged</b>: The complaint filed Monday in Cook County Circuit Court alleges that real estate broker Milan Rubenstein and his company, Slumber Stay LLC, did not properly register his short-term rentals and used a single nontransferable hotel license for multiple listings — then kept renting those units after being issued citations. </p><p><b>The complaint</b>: Airbnb is accused of profiting from those allegedly unlawful rentals rather than working with the city to ensure compliance with the Shared Housing Ordinance. According to the lawsuit, the city issued Rubenstein and Slumber Stay LLC nearly 200 violations in 2024 and 2025. The suit claims Airbnb was aware of those violations but chose to "prioritize profits over compliance with City law."</p><p><b>Key context</b>: The city’s Shared Housing Ordinance limits the number of short-term rentals in a building, restricts short-term rentals in certain neighborhoods and requires registration with the city.</p><p><a class="Link" nobody expected much of it at all," Willems said.</p><p>Two decades-plus and millions of delighted children — and adults — later, Willems has a new picture book adventure featuring the world’s most famous pigeon: "It’s My Bird-Day!"</p><p>Has "The" pigeon learned anything during the last 23 years?</p><p>"Barely," Willems said. "The pigeon is becoming a bit more self aware. The pigeon has made discoveries, like its first name is 'The.'"</p><p>Willems, 58, will be in Chicago Oct. 13 to accept the Chicago Public Library Foundation's Carl Sandburg Literary Award. The annual award honors an author "whose significant body of work has enhanced the public’s awareness of the written word," according to the foundation. entries.title: Car slams into SUV, killing its driver early Tuesday in Lake View
entries.summary: <p>A 52-year-old motorist was killed in a crash early Tuesday in Lake View. </p><p>The man was behind the wheel of a gray SUV at about 3 a.m. in the 1400 block of West Irving Park Road when he tried to make a left turn from a parking lot, Chicago police said.</p><p>Police said the lanes of travel were not clear as the driver proceeded to turn, and a black eastbound car slammed into his SUV, causing the 52-year-old to suffer bodily trauma, police said. </p><p>The man was taken to Illinois Masonic Medical Center, where he was pronounced dead at 5:41 a.m., according to the Cook County medical examiner's office. </p><p>A 47-year-old man had been driving the black car and police said he was not injured and refused medical attention.</p><p>No other injuries were reported, and no citations are pending.</p><p>Area 3 detectives are investigating.<br></p>

entries.title: No más un deporte 'extranjero', finalmente más estadounidenses entienden el fútbol
entries.summary: <p>Ninguno de los aficionados locales a los deportes a quienes conozco desde 1994 mostró mucho interés en la Copa del Mundo.</p><p>Yo ni siquiera sabía que existía un torneo así o que <a class="Link" href="https://www.wttw.com/playlist/2026/06/11/soldier-field-1994-fifa-world-cup" target="_blank" >Chicago</a> estaba entre los anfitriones ese año hasta que un tío de la India me mencionó a mí y a mis hermanos en una breve nota escrita en inglés al final de una postal redactada en urdu dirigida a mi madre.</p><p>La languidez de la persecución policial en la Ford Bronco blanca que transportaba a O.J. Simpson y Al Cowlings probablemente <a class="Link" href="https://www.nytimes.com/athletic/6844638/2026/06/11/world-cup-1994-oj-simpson/" target="_blank" >desvió mi atención</a> de la <a class="Link" href="https://www.nytimes.com/athletic/6757908/2026/06/09/diana-ross-penalty-1994-world-cup/" target="_blank" >ceremonia de apertura</a> hace 32 años en Soldier Field, donde Oprah Winfrey se cayó del escenario y Diana Ross falló un penalti programado mientras cantaba "I'm Coming Out".</p><div class="RichTextSidebarModule Enhancement" data-module data-align-center><a class="AnchorLink" id="module-650000" name="module-650000"></a> <div class="RichTextModule-items RichTextBody"><h3>La Voz Chicago WhatsApp</h3>Encuentra más noticias en nuestro canal de WhatsApp. <a class="Link" href="https://www.whatsapp.com/channel/0029Vb0XT1XCHDylm3rCs40P" target="_blank" ><b>Síguenos.</b></a></div> </div><p>Pero tampoco recuerdo los posteriores partidos de la Copa del Mundo que se jugaron en el campo de los Bears y en otros ocho estadios a través del país tras las festividades del 17 de junio de 1994 y el partido inaugural entre Alemania y Bolivia.</p><p>Estoy segura de que los dioses del fútbol estaban sancionando todo tipo de faltas en mí y en la mayoría de los estadounidenses que eran <a class="Link" href="https://www.nytimes.com/1994/06/17/IHT-the-world-cup-begins-today-in-us-before-an-ambivalent-home-audience.html" target="_blank" >ignorantes o indiferentes</a> mientras un <a class="Link" href="https://apnews.com/article/world-cup-1994-82aa012dd9a3c94d6c6b4f52ca9b5c16" target="_blank" >récord de 3.59 millones</a> llenaba las gradas.</p><p>Esta vez, estoy menos despistada gracias a mis amigos y familiares amantes del fútbol, así como a la creciente importancia del deporte que me ha ayudado a familiarizarme con Mia Hamm, Megan Rapinoe, Mohamed Salah, <a class="Link" href="https://apnews.com/article/world-cup-argentina-lionel-messi-6bdb86e04ed24187b4321cdeed542d4c" target="_blank" >Lionel Messi</a> y otros grandes del deporte.</p><p>No me malinterpreten. No estoy pegada a mi celular y a mi televisor como dos de mis sobrinos que están viendo la mayor competencia internacional de fútbol masculino cada vez que pueden mientras ocurre en los Estados Unidos, Canadá y México.</p><p>He llegado lejos desde pensar que mi primo hablaba de la Chica Material cuando elogiaba al legendario mediocampista argentino Diego Maradona.</p><h3>Fútbol antes que football</h3><p>Se ha jugado al fútbol de alguna forma en Estados Unidos desde principios de los <a class="Link" href="https://www.ussoccer.com/history/timeline" target="_blank" >1800</a> —mucho antes de 1869, cuando un balón de cuero fue pateado en un campo en <a class="Link" href="https://www.ncaa.com/news/football/article/2017-11-06/college-football-history-heres-when-1st-game-was-played" target="_blank" >Nueva Jersey</a> en un partido que desde entonces ha evolucionado hacia el fútbol americano.</p><p>Pero a diferencia de la NFL, MLB, NBA y NHL, el fútbol profesional ha estado a menudo relegado a un segundo plano como un "deporte extranjero", como lo describió el Sun-Times en un artículo que, de otro modo, era elogioso del primer y único evento en vivo de la Copa del Mundo en Daley, rodeado por el equipo de fútbol masculino de la secundaria Farragut, anuncia la selección de Chicago como ciudad anfitriona para la Copa del Mundo de 1994 en la primavera de 1992.</p></figcaption><span class="line"></span><div class="Figure-credit"><p>Sun-Times files</p></div></div> </figure> </div> </div><p>Unos años antes de ese <a class="Link" href="https://www.npr.org/2026/05/09/nx-s1-5795791/2026-history-soccer-fifa-world-cup-fans" target="_blank" >momento decisivo</a>, el fútbol ocupaba el puesto 67, detrás del arrastre de tractores, en una encuesta sobre los deportes de espectador favoritos del país, según ha afirmado <a class="Link" href="https://www.npr.org/2026/03/17/nx-s1-5750358/we-are-the-world-cup-book-review" target="_blank" >el locutor y autor Roger Bennett</a>.</p><p>Hoy, es un juego completamente diferente.</p><p>El fútbol ha superado al béisbol y ahora es el tercer deporte más popular en EE.UU., detrás del fútbol americano y el baloncesto, según <a class="Link" href="https://share.america.gov/wp-content/uploads/sites/155/2026/06/America-is-now-the-biggest-market-for-international-football-The-Economist.pdf" target="_blank" >The Economist</a>.</p><p>Otro estudio reciente lanzado por <a class="Link" href="https://www.tvtechnology.com/insights/analysis/nielsen-north-american-soccer-fans-jump-to-more-than-136-million" target="_blank" >Nielsen</a> reveló que EE.UU. tiene la cuarta mayor base de aficionados al fútbol en el mundo, con 62.5 millones de seguidores.</p><p>Y dado que la mayoría de estos entusiastas son jóvenes —el 76% de los aficionados al fútbol en EE.UU. son millennials o de la Generación Z— tengo esperanza de que llegará el día en que el fútbol ya no sea "otro" para una multitud asustada por un deporte que es abrazado por multitudes de inmigrantes y querido más allá de nuestras fronteras.</p><p>Tenemos un largo camino por recorrer para alcanzar esa meta. La división y la sospecha aún reinan fuera del campo, demostrando las limitaciones del deporte como agente unificador.</p><h3>Discriminación de la administración de Trump</h3><p>Muchos en EE.UU. pueden ya no odiar el juego. Nuestro gobierno actual simplemente odia a los jugadores, dependiendo de su país de origen.</p><p>Varios participantes de la Copa del Mundo, aficionados y periodistas de varios países, incluidos Haití, Irán, Senegal y Costa de Marfil, han enfrentado restricciones más estrictas de visa o se les ha negado la entrada a EE.UU. por las rigurosas políticas de inmigración y las prohibiciones de viaje de la administración de Trump.</p><p>"Es una forma de segregación que no se identifica como tal, pero la prueba está ahí", dijo Julien Kouadio Adonis, presidente del grupo nacional de aficionados de Costa de Marfil, el Comité Nacional de Apoyo a los Elefantes, <a class="Link" href="https://www.bbc.com/news/articles/cx212p8r28eo" target="_blank" >a la BBC</a>.</p><p>Quizás la amnesia sobre la Copa del Mundo sea algo bueno.</p><p>Bromeo. No quiero que las acciones de algunos "estadounidenses feos" me alejen de lo que Pelé denominó "el juego bonito", un juego que me contaron que mi padre jugaba religiosamente cuando era niño.</p><p>Mi padre nunca mencionó participación en ninguna actividad atlética cuando estaba vivo. Tampoco hablaba mucho sobre el fútbol, excepto para reprender a otros estadounidenses por no referirse al deporte como "fútbol", como lo hace la mayoría de la población global.</p><p>Zain y Elyan, los hijos de mi hermana mayor, son ahora quienes están educando al resto de la familia sobre la terminología, las reglas y las normas adecuadas relacionadas con el fútbol.</p><p>Mi hermana menor y yo, que nos unimos a los hermanos en el <a class="Link" href="https://www.fifamuseum.com/en" target="_blank" >Museo de la FIFA</a> en Zúrich, Suiza, en 2023, siempre nos aseguramos de comprarles playeras de fútbol de los países que visitamos.</p><div class="Enhancement" data-align-center> <div class="Enhancement-item" data-crop=""> <figure class="Figure"><a class="AnchorLink" id="image-66fe37" entries.title: Review: Kim Gordon cements her legacy as one of the coolest women in rock in return to Metro
entries.summary: <p>From Bohemian National Cemetery in 2024 to Metro on Tuesday night, Kim Gordon has found a knack for conjuring spirits when she’s in Chicago.</p><p>This time, it was summoning the ghosts of shows past at the Wrigleyville venue. From 1986-88, Gordon and Sonic Youth were frequent visitors at Metro (the 1987 gig turning into the “Hold That Tiger” live album); they also returned in 2002 for the club’s 20th anniversary slate of shows.</p><p>But for anyone who wasn’t around then — or couldn’t snag tickets — seeing Gordon do her thing Tuesday felt like a second chance to bask in all the noise rock glory and get up close and personal with the woman who has held the crown for the coolest girl in rock the last 45 years.</p><div class="Enhancement" data-align-center> <div class="Enhancement-item" data-crop=""> <figure class="Figure-content"><figcaption class="Figure-caption"><p>Kim Gordon performs at the Metro in Wrigleyville on Tuesday. At the heart of her show was promoting her latest album, “Play Me,” released in March. Gordon and her backing band — guitarist Sarah Register, bassist/synth player Emily Retsas and drummer Madi Vogt — performed the record from beginning to end with no skips.</p></figcaption><span class="line"></span><div class="Figure-credit"><p>Tyler Pasciak LaRiviere/Sun-Times</p></div></div> </figure> </div> </div><p>“It’s nice to be back at Metro,” Gordon shared in one of her few bits of chatter. The other was apologizing for a late start as sound techs tinkered with the backline of instruments that would soon become essential components of the show.</p><p>Fresh off an appearance at the Rock & Roll Hall of Fame in Cleveland on Sunday (a slap in the face since she’s still not in it), Gordon’s legacy was palpable throughout the short but impactful 70-minute show.</p><p>At the heart of it was promoting her latest album, “Play Me,” released in March. Gordon and her young and fearless backing band — guitarist Sarah Register, bassist/synth player Emily Retsas and drummer Madi Vogt — performed the record from beginning to end with no skips, followed by an armful of ripe material from Gordon’s other two solo albums that illuminated the breadth of Gordon’s work as an experimental wunderkind obsessed with challenging the barriers of sound.</p><p>Whereas the “Play Me” title track kicked things off with a jazzy horn-filled breakdown, subsequent numbers “Black Out,” “Busy Bee” and “Subcon” (which could’ve also been called “Subwoofer” for its impenetrable bass) tapped into Gordon’s latest obsession: zoning in on trap beats and hip-hop rhythms set against an industrial dystopia. Or the perfect soundtrack for the album’s alarm ringing about artificial intelligence and fascism. “Dirty Tech” was the dagger, with Gordon sarcastically prodding tech bros to “talk dirty” before skewering them as “white-collar service workers.” A true shero for these times.</p><div class="Enhancement" data-align-center> <div class="Enhancement-item" data-crop=""> <figure class="Figure"><a more straightforward rock numbers. Gordon spent much of the night in a rigid front woman pose with just a mic and unabashed micro-dancing. But when she slung on her guitar and got deep in the weeds of distortion pedals on these tracks (even tying herself up with a tangle of cords for the frenetic chokehold of “Cookie Butter”), she was never more in her element.</p><p>What was most interesting about the night was the packed mixed-gen crowd eating it all up — a testament to Gordon’s staying power in her second act. While Gen X got their fill of repressed memories from the days of Sonic Youth, Gen Z and millennials probably didn’t even remember or care that the band broke up in 2011 as they were squarely focused on modern tracks like the 2024 thrasher “Bye Bye” that recently found unexpected virality on TikTok.</p><p>This theme of fruitful second lives started early with an opening set from The Fiery Furnaces. In the dawn of the 2000s, Oak Park siblings Matthew and Eleanor Friedberger were bastions of a second wave of avant-garde rock. And after a very long lull, they recently reformed the group with fresh eyes. Gone is the once full band setup in lieu of just the two on stage, Matthew on keys and Eleanor on vocals.</p><p>The stripped-back approach favors their material. Matthew’s dramatic playing style adds a theatrical nature, while Eleanor’s crisp delivery, unencumbered by an arsenal of sound, shines a spotlight on the zany lyrical poetry of songs like “Blueberry Boat” or “My Egyptian Grammar,” which Eleanor noted was about the South Side.</p><div class="Enhancement" data-align-center> <div class="Enhancement-item" data-crop=""> <figure class="Figure"><a entries.title: Brooke Fletcher returns to White Sox' TV booth as Steve Stone misses another day
entries.summary: <p>A day after becoming the White Sox’s first female dedicated TV analyst, Chicago Sports Network field reporter Brooke Fletcher was still trying to process it all.</p><p>“It’s been an emotional 10 hours,” she said before Wednesday’s game against the Guardians. “I got home last night and I still felt like my head was kind of spinning. I’m like, ‘Wait, what just happened?’”</p><p>Fletcher filled in Tuesday with Steve Stone out because of an illness and was back at it again on Wednesday, working alongside play-by-play announcer John Schriffen. The White Sox hope to have Stone back on Friday, when they open a three-game series against the Kansas City Royals.</p><p>Fletcher wasn’t the first woman to work a White Sox TV broadcast. Mary Shane spent most of the 1977 season as their play-by-play voice with Harry Caray, Lorn Brown and Jimmy Piersall on WSNS-Channel 44. She also broadcast on WMAQ-AM, adding analysis on both.</p><p>Fletcher joined CHSN in 2025 to cover the White Sox. She is married to San Diego Padres infielder Jake Cronenworth and is the daughter of former White Sox infielder Scott Fletcher.</p><p>“I got a lot of texts and a lot of calls, and I was really appreciative of everybody just being so supportive,” Fletcher said. “It really meant a lot, especially with some women in this industry that I really look up to. Jenny Cavnar, Alanna Rizzo, Melanie Newman reached out.”<br></p>
entries.author: Andrew Seligman

entries.title: Bears announce 10 open practices at Halas Hall for upcoming training camp
entries.summary: <p>The <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/bears" target="_blank" >Bears</a> will open training camp July 29 and plan to hold 10 practices open to the public at Halas Hall. The team announced the dates Wednesday.</p><p>The open dates begin with the third and fourth practices of training camp, July 31 and Aug. 1, and continue with Aug. 4-6, 8-9, 13, 18 and 25.</p><p>Tickets are free, though space is significantly limited at Halas Hall, and will be available on the Bears’ website July 8 at 10 a.m. They typically go within minutes.</p><p>The Bears’ <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/bears/2026/06/22/bears-set-start-of-training-camp-joint-practices-with-bengals-titans" >joint practices on the road</a> with the Bengals (Aug. 20) and Titans (Aug. 27) ahead of their preseason games with those teams also are open to the public, but the host teams control admission.</p><p>Along with the rest of the NFL, the team currently is on break for the summer. Mandatory report day for Bears veterans is July 28, while rookies and quarterbacks will report ahead of that.</p><p>They begin the preseason Aug. 15 at home against the Browns and start the regular season Sept. 13 at the Panthers.</p>
entries.author: Jason Lieser

entries.title: White Sox' series finale vs. Guardians will be delayed
entries.summary: <p>The White Sox' game Wednesday against the Guardians will be delayed because of the weather, the team announced. More information will be released when it's available. First pitch was scheduled for 1:10 p.m.</p><p>The Sox are going for the series sweep after winning Monday 6-5 and Tuesday 2-1. They began the day with a one-game lead over the Guardians for first place in the American League Central.</p><p>Chris Murphy is set to be the opener for the Sox ahead of Erick Fedde. Tanner Bibee is slated to start for the Guardians. </p>
entries.author: Jeff Agrest

entries.title: Ben Brown, Edward Cabrera to IL with Cubs buried in avalanche of pitching injuries: ‘This is crazy’
entries.summary: <p>NEW YORK – When Edward Cabrera officially hit the injured list with a left hamstring strain Wednesday, the <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/cubs" >Cubs</a> had four-fifths of their Opening Day starting rotation and their closer on the shelf.</p><p>It’s hard to win a World Series when dealt that kind of hand.</p><p>And to make a real bad situation even worse, Cabrera wasn’t even the only Cubs starter to hit the IL on Wednesday, with the team putting righty Ben Brown – who’s been excellent in fill-in duty – on the shelf with a neck strain.</p><p>If Cabrera’s visible pain and <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/cubs/2026/06/23/cubs-edward-cabrera-pitching-injuries-rotation-offseason-trade-jed-hoyer-craig-counsell" >trip off the field via cart Tuesday night</a> wasn’t enough to have some fans seeing the Cubs’ season flashing before their eyes, Wednesday’s news surely did the trick.</p><p>Injuries are a part of the game, sure. But this big a part? What team could survive this?</p><p>“It always seems the worst in the present,” injured right-hander Jameson Taillon told the Sun-Times on Wednesday. “I’ve been on teams with a lot of unfortunate injuries, but this is crazy.”</p><p>The Cubs were still waiting on imaging to inform them of the severity of Cabrera’s hamstring strain Wednesday morning.</p><p>Taillon, meanwhile, is still weeks away from his return from a hamstring injury. Righty Cade Horton is done for the year with Tommy John surgery. And team president Jed Hoyer, in a Tuesday radio interview, threw cold water on the idea of lefty Justin Steele making a return to the rotation this season.</p><p>“We’re in a rough spot,” manager Craig Counsell said in the immediate wake of Cabrera’s injury Tuesday night.</p><p>There has been positive word on Taillon’s progress, and lefty Matthew Boyd will <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/cubs/2026/06/22/cubs-matthew-boyd-injury-injured-list-next-start-rotation-craig-counsell-seiya-suzuki-knee-right-field-matt-shaw-pete-crow-armstrong-player-of-the-week" >make his long-awaited return from the IL on Thursday</a> to pitch in the series finale with the Mets.</p><p>Boyd’s back, a much needed reinforcement, and left-hander Shota Imanaga has returned to form after an ugly stretch. The rest of the puzzle, though, must be completed with fill-in pieces.</p><p>Brown was already that, stepping in from the bullpen to post the best pitching numbers on the team. Coming into Wednesday, his 1.85 ERA was the fifth best in baseball among pitchers with at least 60 innings.</p><p>Fellow right-hander Javier Assad has been very effective in three straight outings since returning from the minor leagues, with just two runs allowed in 18 innings.</p><p>But righty Colin Rea, who potentially could have returned to the bullpen upon Boyd’s return, will now have to stay in the rotation with Cabrera and Brown on the shelf. Will he return to the version who excelled in substitute duty a season ago? <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/cubs/2026/06/15/cubs-colin-rea-starting-pitching-rotation-injuries-craig-counsell-matthew-boyd" >The Cubs need him to</a>.</p><p>The options beyond the major league roster? There don’t seem to be too many good ones, with only lefty Jordan Wicks springing to mind as an obvious candidate. Wicks was quickly jettisoned back to the minor leagues after a brief big league cameo in which he gave up 11 runs in 6 1/3 innings.</p><p>Wednesday call-up Vince Velasquez might now be forced into at least a temporary rotation spot with Brown and Cabrera both going down with injuries.</p><p>It puts the onus on Hoyer’s front office to bolster the pitching staff before the trade deadline in early August. But will a wildly depleted pitching staff hang on long enough to keep the Cubs in buy mode?</p><p>To that point, whether or not you think the Cubs are still capable of catching the Brewers and making a deep October run with their gigantic stack of pitching injuries, they still have to play games for the next three and a half months, quite a significant chunk of the baseball calendar.</p><p>“Look, man, a lot of bad stuff’s happened. We get to make our own story from it,” Counsell said before Wednesday’s doubleheader. “And it gets a little tougher. But stack the chips against us, whatever you want to say. That’s fine.</p><p>“Circle the wagons, let’s go. These are our guys. That’s the attitude you take, and it’s what we’re going to try to do.”</p>
entries.author: Vinnie Duber

entries.title: Sacan a Edward Cabrera del campo, empeorando la situación para los Cubs en lesiones de lanzadores
entries.summary: <p>NUEVA YORK – Justo cuando pensabas que no podía empeorar para el cuerpo de lanzadores golpeado de los <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/cubs" target="_blank" >Cubs</a>, sí empeoró.</p><p>El abridor derecho Edward Cabrera salió en camilla tras sufrir una distensión en el isquiotibial/aductor izquierdo durante la victoria de 9-6 sobre los Mets el martes por la noche, mientras cubría la primera base en un rodado que terminó en la quinta entrada.</p><p>Los Cubs conocerán más sobre la gravedad de la lesión este miércoles, pero el manager Craig Counsell dijo que Cabrera irá a la lista de lesionados.</p><div class="RichTextSidebarModule Enhancement" data-module data-align-center><a class="AnchorLink" id="module-710000" name="module-710000"></a> <div class="RichTextModule-items RichTextBody"><h3>La Voz Chicago WhatsApp</h3>Encuentra más noticias en nuestro canal de WhatsApp. <a class="Link" href="https://www.whatsapp.com/channel/0029Vb0XT1XCHDylm3rCs40P" target="_blank" ><b>Síguenos.</b></a></div> </div><p>Es otra mala noticia para los Cubs, que ya tenían a tres integrantes de su rotación abridora del Día Inaugural en la lista de lesionados: el zurdo Matthew Boyd y los diestros Cade Horton y Jameson Taillon. Aunque se espera que Boyd <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/cubs/2026/06/22/cubs-matthew-boyd-injury-injured-list-next-start-rotation-craig-counsell-seiya-suzuki-knee-right-field-matt-shaw-pete-crow-armstrong-player-of-the-week" target="_blank" >regrese en los próximos días</a>, Cabrera, aunque sea brevemente, los convertirá en cuatro.</p><p>No se espera que Taillon regrese en las próximas semanas, y Horton ha terminado su temporada. Para empeorar las cosas, el presidente del equipo, Jed Hoyer, dijo en una entrevista de radio el martes que es "poco realista" esperar que el zurdo Justin Steele, quien está fuera desde el inicio de la temporada pasada, inicie juegos para el equipo este año.</p><p>“Estamos en una situación difícil”, comentó Counsell. “Creo que podemos salir adelante. Se trata del receso del Juego de Estrellas [donde las cosas serán más desafiantes]. Va a ser un poco de rompecabezas hasta entonces”.</p><p>Los diestros Ben Brown y Javier Assad han sido una especie de salvadores como rellenos de la rotación. El diestro Colin Rea <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/cubs/2026/06/15/cubs-colin-rea-starting-pitching-rotation-injuries-craig-counsell-matthew-boyd" target="_blank" >no ha estado tan bien</a> como estuvo en su labor de suplente la temporada pasada. Si los Cubs necesitan apoyarse en su profundidad aún más, no está claro cuántas buenas opciones tienen.</p><p>Los abridores de los Cubs llegaron el martes con un promedio de efectividad de 4.62, el séptimo más alto en el béisbol.</p><p>“Hemos tenido muchas lesiones y hemos tenido que hacer que algunos jugadores se hagan cargo”, dijo Hoyer la semana pasada en Wrigley Field. “Sí, las adiciones externas a la rotación son una posibilidad, no tanto ahora como más adelante. Pero esa parte de nuestro equipo que está luchando, honestamente, es algo lógico dado lo que nos falta.</p><p>“Hay algunos chicos que han dado un paso al frente, pero vamos a necesitar más de eso. Incluso si la ofensiva comienza a funcionar, vamos a necesitar más consistencia de ese grupo”, agregó.</p><p>Cabrera era uno de los lanzadores que debía dar un paso al frente; los Cubs aún esperando ver la mejor versión del derecho que trajeron el invierno pasado, esperando que estaban incorporando a un tipo de lanzador de primera línea para el lado norte.</p><p>Fue el tipo de cambio que la oficina principal de Hoyer <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/cubs/2025/07/31/2025-trade-deadline-cubs-prez-jed-hoyer-balks-at-asking-price-for-frontline-starter-adds-four-players" target="_blank" >no hizo en la fecha límite de cambios del año pasado</a>, cuando el presidente del equipo optó por mantener sus piezas futuras en lugar de complementar un cuerpo de lanzadores golpeado. El movimiento en la temporada baja fue parte de establecer expectativas de nivel de campeonatos para el equipo de los Cubs de este año.</p><p>Pero en sus primeras 14 aperturas con el uniforme de los Cubs, Cabrera tiene un promedio de efectividad de 5.10, mucho más alto que el 3.53 que registró la temporada pasada con los Marlins. Esos resultados de 2025 fueron lo suficientemente atractivos como para convencer a Hoyer y compañía de hacer de Cabrera una parte clave de los planes de lanzadores de la organización de cara al futuro.</p><p>¿Los resultados hasta ahora esta temporada? Son poco atractivos.</p><p>Después de un par de salidas flojas a principios de este mes, Cabrera permitió solo dos carreras el martes antes de la lesión. Pero tuvo algunos momentos problemáticos, incluyendo una segunda entrada difícil en la que hizo caminar a tres y permitió un par de imparables, incluido un hit productor de dos carreras, todo esto con dos outs.</p><p>Los resultados deben ser mejores, pero ahora la pregunta es qué tipo de oportunidad tendrá Cabrera después de sufrir la lesión el martes, otra mala noticia para un cuerpo de lanzadores que ha sido golpeado por lesiones.</p><p>“Entramos a la temporada pensando que teníamos números reales. El juego moderno se encarga de eso rápidamente, y realmente ha puesto a prueba nuestra profundidad”, dijo Hoyer. “Las lesiones son parte del juego, son parte del desafío.</p><p>“En algunas temporadas se puede soportar un poco, y en otras no. Y nosotros no hemos podido”.</p><p><i>Traducido con una herramienta de inteligencia artificial (AI) y editado por </i><a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/la-voz" target="_blank" ><i>La Voz Chicago</i></a><br></p>
entries.author: Vinnie Duber

entries.title: Metra designer unveils special locomotive ahead of nation's 250th birthday: 'This is America'
entries.summary: <p>Not too busy, a little bit unique and something that screams Metra. That's what graphic designer Falecia Woods envisioned when she was tasked with creating a special Metra locomotive to celebrate the nation's 250th birthday. </p><p>The locomotive was showcased during a media briefing Wednesday morning at the Metra Western Avenue Coach Yard, 2801 W. Grand Ave. in Humboldt Park, where senior graphic designer Woods described her inspiration: a chance to turn a traditional commuter train into a moving piece of artwork.</p><p>"I wanted something that was — as it's going down the track — easily recognizable, not too busy, but something a little bit unique," Woods said during the briefing. "You rarely get a graphic designer, especially in-house, to design a train from start to finish by yourself."</p><p>Woods, an artist with more than 30 years of experience, also designed Metra's Veterans Day locomotive in 2024. Woods said that she was challenged by the <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/arts-and-culture/2026/04/02/america-250-illinois-chicago-federal-national-endowment-arts-trump" target="_blank" >America 250 project</a>, to create something that would be instantly recognizable as it traveled throughout Chicago.</p><p>The locomotive's patriotic colors and design, inspired by the American flag, was styled differently than the Veterans Day locomotive. Woods intentionally made both sides of the America 250 locomotive identical so onlookers could get the same visual impact from either direction.</p><p>"You see it at a glance," she said. "You can usually recognize the red, white, and blue. The sense of this is America."</p><div class="Enhancement" data-align-center> <div class="Enhancement-item" data-crop=""> <figure class="Figure"><a class="AnchorLink" id="image-500000" entries.title: Bowen Byram believes he can become a No. 1 defenseman, and the Blackhawks need him to be right
entries.summary: <p>On each of his first two NHL teams, new <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/blackhawks?_gl=1*1ehmini*_up*MQ..*_ga*Njk5MDk5NDY1LjE3ODIzMzE1MDI.*_ga_K0F0MB46T8*czE3ODIzMzE1MDEkbzEkZzAkdDE3ODIzMzE1MTEkajUwJGwwJGgw" target="_blank" >Blackhawks</a> defenseman Bowen Byram was stuck behind a superstar who blocked him from becoming a No. 1 defenseman.</p><p>With the Avalanche, it was Cale Makar. With the Sabres, it was Rasmus Dahlin.</p><p>On the Hawks, Byram will have no such hindrance — and he is, in fact, expected to develop into a No. 1 defenseman. Hawks general manager Kyle Davidson wouldn't have <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/blackhawks/2026/06/23/blackhawks-bowen-byram-trade-sabres-kyle-davidson-louis-crevier-analysis?_gl=1*1pqh72o*_up*MQ..*_ga*MTA1NDg1Nzk4Mi4xNzgyMzI1OTA5*_ga_K0F0MB46T8*czE3ODIzMjU5MDgkbzEkZzAkdDE3ODIzMjU5MDgkajYwJGwwJGgw" target="_blank" >traded</a> the fourth overall pick if he didn't foresee that as a likelihood.</p><p>Byram knows that, too.</p><p>"I'm just scratching the surface of what I can do," Byram said Wednesday. "I'm really excited for this opportunity because it’s going to be a chance for me to blossom into the player I think I can be."</p><p>Asked about Makar and Dahlin, he added that he's also gleaned lessons from other strong former defensive teammates in Devon Toews, Josh Manson, Owen Power and Mattias Samuelsson.</p><p>The fact he has always been surrounded by so much established talent isn't necessarily a bad thing, especially since that won't be the case on the Hawks. Now those support systems are gone — and so are the shackles on his ice time.</p><p>"I can't get too carried away," Byram said. "I have to come in and prove what I can do. I'm confident in myself. I feel that, after this move, the Blackhawks are confident in me, too. It's a great feeling to have a team believing in you."</p><p>Davidson very much needs Byram to be right about the potential he possesses. This trade represents a massive risk. It's not dramatic to say the overall rebuild's success now partially depends on Byram's success. </p><p>And the hockey world doesn't share much of the Hawks' internal confidence that this gamble will pay off. This trade, and Davidson's asset management as a whole, has been mocked by many critics over the past two days. Davidson plans to hold out for the last laugh.</p><p>"We’re going to provide him the opportunity to become one of the top defensemen around the league, and we feel 100% wholehearted that he can and will be that guy," Davidson said Wednesday. "So when you take it like that...there aren’t many pieces around the league that are more valuable.</p><p>"The natural progression of his game is going to find that value for us in the transaction."</p><p>Davidson also believes Byram himself can take over a Dahlin-esque role by sheltering and helping develop young Hawks defensemen like Artyom Levshunov and Sam Rinzel.</p><p>Byram did average more than 22 minutes per game during each of his two full seasons with the Sabres, but he never quarterbacked their top power-play unit. That's another key role he will take over immediately with the Hawks.</p><p>Although some of the heat on Davidson has centered on him not using his most valuable trade chip to acquire a proven winger to accompany Connor Bedard, the Hawks expect Byram's offensive abilities to benefit Bedard in less obvious yet still effective ways.</p><p>"I break the puck out well, I move the puck well and I think I’ll get the puck into the hands of our forwards quickly and efficiently," Byram said. "That’s really important: You want your skilled forwards having the puck and creating and attacking."</p><p>Byram and Bedard, as two British Columbia natives, are already friends. Bedard called Byram on Tuesday night — reportedly from a golf course — to express his excitement about the trade.</p><p>Byram is left-handed but has experience playing on both sides, which adds flexibility to the Hawks' defensive lineup alongside Levshunov, Rinzel, Alex Vlasic, Wyatt Kaiser and Kevin Korchinski. The Hawks could still sign a veteran free-agent defenseman like Jacob Trouba or Mario Ferraro.</p><p>"I want to come to Chicago and help the team make the playoffs," Byram said. "My experience in Buffalo showed me it can happen very quickly if everyone is on the same page."</p><h3><b>Contract talks </b></h3><p>The focus now shifts to Byram's contract situation. He's currently a year away from unrestricted free agency, and he will become extension-eligible next Wednesday — the opening day of 2026 free agency.</p><p>"We'll have to put our money where our mouth is...because we believe in this guy," Davidson said. "We’re OK paying great players. If there’s an opportunity to acquire and retain a player that we believe is elite and a star, then we will do so and won’t blink in doing it."</p><p>Byram claimed there haven't been any contract talks yet with the Hawks, but he emphasized that he "plans on being in Chicago for a long time," calling it "the place I wanted to end up."</p><p>He explained he grew up a Hawks fan because his dad, Shawn, was a minor-league journeyman who played one game for the Hawks in 1991-92, as well as because he saw the dynasty Hawks beat his hometown Canucks so often as a kid.</p><p>He wanted the Hawks to draft him with the No. 3 pick in 2019, but they took Kirby Dach instead — foolishly, in retrospect. The Avalanche snagged him at No. 4.</p><p>"It's funny how things have come full circle," Byram said.</p><p>Sabres GM Jarmo Kekalainen told reporters Wednesday in Buffalo that Byram never engaged in contract talks with the Sabres this past season because he was focused on becoming a No. 1 defenseman somewhere.</p><p>Now that he has that title, there's a strong chance his salary-cap hit will top $10 million — a threshold only four other defensemen around the league (Dahlin being one) currently exceed.</p><h3><b>Forward question</b></h3><p>Trade prices around the NHL are astronomical, and it sounds like the package the Hawks traded for Byram — the fourth and 45th picks plus Louis Crevier — would not have been enough to pry winger Matthew Knies out of Toronto.</p><p>The Hawks would've had to include a young core player like Levshunov, Rinzel, Vlasic or Anton Frondell to make that trade a reality, and they justifiably weren't willing to pay that price.</p><p>Davidson mentioned the Hawks still have many other assets to offer in trade proposals, including three 2027 first-round picks, and they continue to scour the forward market. But he said they're comfortable moving ahead with incoming Russian rookie Roman Kantserov as Bedard's designated winger for next season if nothing comes to fruition.</p><p>"Maybe if we traded for Roman instead of just signing him, it would be more exciting and people would accept it as an option more than they currently do," Davidson quipped.</p><p>Meanwhile, free agent-to-be Ilya Mikheyev is likely heading to open market. Physical veteran forward Jordan Greenway, acquired Tuesday along with Byram, could take over some of Mikheyev's penalty-killing duties.</p>

entries.title: Severe thunderstorm warning issued for Cook County
entries.summary: <p>A severe thunderstorm warning was issued Wednesday evening for northwest Cook County, according to the National Weather Service.</p><p>It was set to expire at 7:15 p.m. A tornado warning was put in place for about an hour in northeastern Kane County and northwestern Cook County; it expired at 6:45 p.m.</p><p>Quarter-sized hail and 70 mph winds, as well as "widespread tree damage," were reported in Bartlett around 6:36 p.m., according to the weather service. The storms were moving from Wisconsin southeast into the metro area and toward the city.</p><p>A severe thunderstorm watch remained in effect for Cook, DeKalb, DuPage, Grundy, Kane, Kankakee, Kendall, LaSalle, Lake, McHenry and Will counties until 10 p.m.</p>

entries.title: Chicago teens testify about takeovers — ‘How can we better make adults our role models?’
entries.summary: <p>A group of Chicago teens traded their summer plans for government business Wednesday to testify about “teen trends” and implore City Council members to think beyond curfew ordinances when trying to stop the large gatherings from turning violent.</p><p>“Just imagine if we had an entire City Council that's supporting youth with the same energy that they have going against youth,” said Damarrion Spann, a youth leader at My Block My Hood My City.</p><p>Spann was one of five youth organizers invited to a subject matter hearing that comes as the topic of "teen takeovers," large gatherings of young people summoned by social media that sometimes turn unruly and violent, again garners the attention of residents and politicians, including President Donald Trump.</p><p>Numerous teen trends have led to high-profile, tragic incidents of violence, in part because of the ease of access youth have to guns. City officials say many large gatherings also go without incident. Chicago police track teen trends, in part by monitoring flyers on social media advertising the get-togethers. Chicago’s Deputy Mayor for Community Safety, Emmanuel Andre, said Wednesday that 49 teen trends are expected to take place, or already have taken place, in June alone.</p><p>But despite the dominating role the topic plays in City Council debates over how to thwart violence, the teens spoke to a largely empty Council chamber Wednesday, with many of the 15-member Subcommittee on Youth Employment absent.</p><div class="RelatedList Enhancement" data-module data-align-center> <div class="RelatedList-title">Related</div> <ul class="RelatedList-items"> <li class="RelatedList-items-item"> <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/city-hall/2026/05/27/mayor-brandon-johnson-teen-takeovers-hyde-park-near-west-side-memorial-day-weekend-curfew-parent-responsibility-laws" >Mayor Johnson still opposed to stricter curfew and parent responsibility laws after holiday weekend mayhem</a> </li> </ul> </div> <p>About three to seven alderpersons filtered in and out of the chamber throughout the roughly three-hour meeting, with some joining virtually. The scant audience didn’t go unnoticed.</p><p>“Some aldermen are just not ready to be in a shared space with youth, and that's totally unacceptable,” Spann said.</p><p>The low attendance rate didn’t cause the teens to hold back. They lobbied for the city to invest in physical spaces where they can go with adults who can, in essence, be more kidlike.</p><p>“It's not that the youth wants to throw out adults completely, it's that we just want adults that work with us and understand us, and are able to regress to their own youth in order to do that,” said Jailyn Mendez, 18, a youth leader with the Puerto Rican Cultural Center.</p><p>Kids shared what they’d want in a dream community center: live DJ sets, free food, homework help and extracurriculars you don’t get in school, like budgeting tips or craft workshops. They testified about everything from their favorite social media platforms to what restaurants they want the city to partner with for events.</p><p>“I can’t really answer the food questions because I don’t really eat much. I usually go for fries. But the apps ... usually TikTok, for real,” said Deja Williams, 18, who lives in West Englewood.</p><p>Williams said most days after school he goes straight home “not because I don’t want to be outside” but “because there are few places to go” and “you often have to worry about violence and whether you will be safe or if you will be profiled or harassed.”</p><p>Most of the Council members present were progressives or Democratic Socialists who have long railed against stricter curfews as a way to solve violent gatherings.</p><p>Ald. Pat Dowell (3rd) is not a Democratic Socialist and voted in favor of a stricter curfew ordinance that passed the City Council last summer, but failed to survive a <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/city-hall/2025/07/16/snap-curfew-veto-upheld-mayor-johnson-city-council-vote" >mayoral veto.</a> </p><p></p><p></p><p>Dowell said she was grateful to hear from youth, but wanted a more “balanced” hearing on the topic that includes Chicago police, the park and school districts and parents.</p><p>“This is an important topic, and we really can't sugarcoat it,” she said, citing a recent gathering where she says police recovered 53 guns. “We don't talk about the problems that our good kids might be covering for some of the bad kids that are integrating into those events.”</p><p>Ald. Jessie Fuentes (26th), who chaired the hearing, said she wanted to “center the voices of young people” at the first of a series of hearings this summer on teen takeovers, and that the police department will be represented in the future.</p><div class="Enhancement" data-align-center> <div class="Enhancement-item" data-crop=""> <figure class="Figure"><a class="AnchorLink" id="image-8f0000" name="image-8f0000"></a> <picture data-crop="medium"> <source type="image/webp" width="490" height="275" data-srcset="https://cst.brightspotcdn.com/dims4/default/7883d23/2147483647/strip/true/crop/6052x3397+0+320/resize/490x275!/format/webp/quality/90/?url=https%3A%2F%2Fchorus-production-cst-web.s3.us-east-1.amazonaws.com%2Fbrightspot%2Fb5%2Fe1%2Fd8cafaa540ae89ce3e144b850abf%2Fcounciltakeovers-260625-21.jpg 1x,https://cst.brightspotcdn.com/dims4/default/26ef2e7/2147483647/strip/true/crop/6052x3397+0+320/resize/980x550!/format/webp/quality/90/?url=https%3A%2F%2Fchorus-production-cst-web.s3.us-east-1.amazonaws.com%2Fbrightspot%2Fb5%2Fe1%2Fd8cafaa540ae89ce3e144b850abf%2Fcounciltakeovers-260625-21.jpg 2x" data-lazy-load="true" srcset="data:image/svg+xml;base64,PHN2ZyB4bWxucz0iaHR0cDovL3d3dy53My5vcmcvMjAwMC9zdmciIHZlcnNpb249IjEuMSIgaGVpZ2h0PSIyNzVweCIgd2lkdGg9IjQ5MHB4Ij48L3N2Zz4=" /> <source width="490" height="275" data-srcset="https://cst.brightspotcdn.com/dims4/default/b4ab569/2147483647/strip/true/crop/6052x3397+0+320/resize/490x275!/quality/90/?url=https%3A%2F%2Fchorus-production-cst-web.s3.us-east-1.amazonaws.com%2Fbrightspot%2Fb5%2Fe1%2Fd8cafaa540ae89ce3e144b850abf%2Fcounciltakeovers-260625-21.jpg" data-lazy-load="true" srcset="data:image/svg+xml;base64,PHN2ZyB4bWxucz0iaHR0cDovL3d3dy53My5vcmcvMjAwMC9zdmciIHZlcnNpb249IjEuMSIgaGVpZ2h0PSIyNzVweCIgd2lkdGg9IjQ5MHB4Ij48L3N2Zz4=" /> <img class="Image" alt="Ald. Jessie Fuentes (26th) discusses “teen takeovers” while presiding over a meeting of the Chicago City Council’s Subcommittee on Youth Employment at City Hall, Wednesday, June 24, 2026. " srcset="https://cst.brightspotcdn.com/dims4/default/b4ab569/2147483647/strip/true/crop/6052x3397+0+320/resize/490x275!/quality/90/?url=https%3A%2F%2Fchorus-production-cst-web.s3.us-east-1.amazonaws.com%2Fbrightspot%2Fb5%2Fe1%2Fd8cafaa540ae89ce3e144b850abf%2Fcounciltakeovers-260625-21.jpg 1x,https://cst.brightspotcdn.com/dims4/default/433cff3/2147483647/strip/true/crop/6052x3397+0+320/resize/980x550!/quality/90/?url=https%3A%2F%2Fchorus-production-cst-web.s3.us-east-1.amazonaws.com%2Fbrightspot%2Fb5%2Fe1%2Fd8cafaa540ae89ce3e144b850abf%2Fcounciltakeovers-260625-21.jpg 2x" width="490" height="275" data-src="https://cst.brightspotcdn.com/dims4/default/b4ab569/2147483647/strip/true/crop/6052x3397+0+320/resize/490x275!/quality/90/?url=https%3A%2F%2Fchorus-production-cst-web.s3.us-east-1.amazonaws.com%2Fbrightspot%2Fb5%2Fe1%2Fd8cafaa540ae89ce3e144b850abf%2Fcounciltakeovers-260625-21.jpg" data-lazy-load="true" src="data:image/svg+xml;base64,PHN2ZyB4bWxucz0iaHR0cDovL3d3dy53My5vcmcvMjAwMC9zdmciIHZlcnNpb249IjEuMSIgaGVpZ2h0PSIyNzVweCIgd2lkdGg9IjQ5MHB4Ij48L3N2Zz4=" > </picture> <div class="Figure-content"><figcaption class="Figure-caption"><p>Ald. Jessie Fuentes (26th) discusses “teen takeovers” while presiding over a meeting of the Chicago City Council’s Subcommittee on Youth Employment at City Hall, Wednesday.</p></figcaption><span class="line"></span><div class="Figure-credit"><p>Ashlee Rezin/Sun-Times</p></div></div> </figure> </div> </div><p>Dowell’s testimony sparked some backlash from the panel and impassioned closing remarks from Romya Simone, a Communities United youth leader. She urged Council members to view teen violence as a symptom, not a cause, of societal woes.</p><p>“If we were to have a curfew, that's not going to stop the gun violence from happening. ... How are these young people getting 53 guns? There are adults who are selling these guns to young people. So how can we better make adults our role models?” Simone asked.</p><p>Afterward, she said that having Chicago police at the hearings “would be very helpful,” but bristled at the idea of “good” and “bad” kids.</p><p>“The teens that were here today, we were labeled as we are the 'good kids,’ representing the 'bad kids’ for our community, and that made me feel unheard. We are just kids … We are a reflection of our city. That means we get what the city pours into us,” she said.</p><p>“If the city is pouring into guns and disinvestments, then that's what we're going to represent,” Simone said.</p>

Visit <a class="Link" href="http://mcachicago.org" target="_blank" ><u>mcachicago.org</u></a>.</li></ul><div class="Enhancement" data-align-center> <div class="Enhancement-item" data-crop=""> <figure class="Figure"><a class="AnchorLink" id="image-be0000" name="image-be0000"></a> <picture data-crop="medium"> <source type="image/webp" width="490" height="275" data-srcset="https://cst.brightspotcdn.com/dims4/default/ae48eda/2147483647/strip/true/crop/4032x2263+0+381/resize/490x275!/format/webp/quality/90/?url=https%3A%2F%2Fchorus-production-cst-web.s3.us-east-1.amazonaws.com%2Fbrightspot%2F34%2F98%2F411eb4804ebe8dfef95af7674eb4%2Fempty-vessels-no-5-a-painting-by-marya-veeck-courtesy-of-the-artist.jpg 1x,https://cst.brightspotcdn.com/dims4/default/3945080/2147483647/strip/true/crop/4032x2263+0+381/resize/980x550!/format/webp/quality/90/?url=https%3A%2F%2Fchorus-production-cst-web.s3.us-east-1.amazonaws.com%2Fbrightspot%2F34%2F98%2F411eb4804ebe8dfef95af7674eb4%2Fempty-vessels-no-5-a-painting-by-marya-veeck-courtesy-of-the-artist.jpg 2x" data-lazy-load="true" srcset="data:image/svg+xml;base64,PHN2ZyB4bWxucz0iaHR0cDovL3d3dy53My5vcmcvMjAwMC9zdmciIHZlcnNpb249IjEuMSIgaGVpZ2h0PSIyNzVweCIgd2lkdGg9IjQ5MHB4Ij48L3N2Zz4=" /> <source width="490" height="275" data-srcset="https://cst.brightspotcdn.com/dims4/default/ec1f55e/2147483647/strip/true/crop/4032x2263+0+381/resize/490x275!/quality/90/?url=https%3A%2F%2Fchorus-production-cst-web.s3.us-east-1.amazonaws.com%2Fbrightspot%2F34%2F98%2F411eb4804ebe8dfef95af7674eb4%2Fempty-vessels-no-5-a-painting-by-marya-veeck-courtesy-of-the-artist.jpg" data-lazy-load="true" srcset="data:image/svg+xml;base64,PHN2ZyB4bWxucz0iaHR0cDovL3d3dy53My5vcmcvMjAwMC9zdmciIHZlcnNpb249IjEuMSIgaGVpZ2h0PSIyNzVweCIgd2lkdGg9IjQ5MHB4Ij48L3N2Zz4=" /> <img class="Image" alt="Empty Vessels No. 5 - entries.title: Bally's offers to substitute airport slot machines for video gambling terminals
entries.summary: <p>Bally’s offered Wednesday to move quickly to install lounges filled with <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/casinos-gambling/2025/10/21/slot-machines-ohare-midway-airports-city-council" >slot machines at O’Hare and Midway </a>airports and “substitute” that revenue for the $6.8 million the city was counting on by lifting the ban on video gambling terminals.</p><p>Christopher Jewett, senior vice president for corporate development at Bally’s, said each of the four passenger terminals at O’Hare as well as the one at Midway could support one slot machine lounge.</p><p>“We believe one lounge can generate approximately $5 million in actual gaming and admission taxes, which go directly to the city,” Jewett told the City Council’s Committee on Workforce Development. “This alone can replace the revenue in question.”</p><p>The $16.6 billion 2026 budget <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/city-hall/2025/12/23/mayor-brandon-johnson-city-council-alternate-budget" target="_blank" >approved by a City Council </a>majority lifted the Chicago ban on video gambling and assumed Chicago would generate $6.8 million by licensing newly legalized <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/city-hall/2025/09/16/video-gaming-in-chicago-proposal-anthony-beale-brandon-johnson" target="_blank" >video gambling terminals</a> across the city.</p><p>That’s based on the assumption that 80% of the 3,300 eligible establishments with off-premise liquor licenses will apply, but also that the Illinois Gaming Board would take six to eight months to grant those licenses.</p><p>Ald. Anthony Beale (9th), a strong City Council advocate for legalizing video gambling terminals, said the Illinois General Assembly authorized Bally’s to install airport slot machines years ago and the gaming giant has, so far, failed to take advantage of it.</p><p>Beale also argued that revenue raised at O’Hare and Midway must remain in the enterprise fund that supports airport operations. So repealing the ordinance that authorized video gambling would still leave the City Council with a budget hole to fill.</p><p>Mayor Brandon Johnson asked his ally, Workforce Development Chair and 22nd Ward Ald. Mike Rodriguez to hold Wednesday’s hearing to lay the groundwork to repeal the ordinance authorizing Chicago bars, restaurants and bowling alleys to install video gambling terminals.</p><p>Beale asked Business Affairs and Consumer Protection Commissioner Ivan Capifali why he has allowed 7,000 sweepstakes machines to operate illegally in Chicago. </p><p><a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/city-hall/2026/06/17/ald-anthony-beale-sweepstakes-machines-ban-fails-chicago-city-council-video-gambling-terminals" >Sweepstakes machines </a>look like video slot machines but have managed to operate in a gray area of the law by offering “free play” options and coupons to winners instead of cash.</p><p>“I would like not to discuss sweepstakes machines in this forum. I am not going into gambling policy debates with you or anybody in this forum,” Capifali said. “The point of my statement was the implementation burdens that this ordinance, without BACP at the table, brought to us. That’s all I’m here to debate and to argue. I am not talking about sweepstakes or anything around VGTs.”</p><p>Beale then unloaded on Capifali before bringing Wednesday’s hearing to an abrupt halt.</p><p>“Ivan, you make excuses left and right. Your integrity is zero. You have none. ... Ivan, commissioner, I believe that you need to resign because you are doing a disservice to the city of Chicago,” Beale said.</p><p>After accusing Johnson of going around the License Committee, whose chair supports video gambling, Beale said, “I motion that we adjourn this meeting because it’s not appropriate.” </p><p>The meeting then ended. </p><p></p><p>The decision to lift the Chicago ban on video gambling terminals has divided the City Council and exacerbated tensions between alderpersons and Johnson.</p><p>Bally’s has warned repeatedly that lifting Chicago’s<a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/city-hall/2025/09/16/video-gaming-in-chicago-proposal-anthony-beale-brandon-johnson" target="_blank" > ban on video gambling </a>would cost the cash-strapped city $74 million in annual revenue and up to 1,050 jobs at its temporary and permanent casinos.</p><p>The casino giant has further warned that lifting the long-standing Chicago ban would force the Johnson administration to renegotiate “critical elements” of its host agreement, wipe out a yearly $4 million lump-sum payment from Bally’s and shrink the casino jackpot needed to save police and fire pension funds.</p><p>Johnson has raised strong objections to legalizing video gambling, in part because he said he believes it would violate the city’s host agreement with Bally’s, which is operating a temporary casino at Medinah Temple while building a permanent casino-entertainment complex in River West.</p><p>The mayor’s City Council allies have either banned or attempted to ban video gambling terminals in their individual wards while buying time for Johnson to find the votes to repeal the ordinance citywide.</p><p>Before Wednesday's adjournment, Jewett argued that Bally's signed the host agreement on the assumption that the city would "adhere to its long-standing agreement to prohibit VGTs."</p><p>"Had we known that, within just a few years, this body would reverse course and allow an alternative form of gambling that breaches the agreement, we would never agree to the numerous commitments, all of which we've held up," he said.</p><p>License Chair and 50th Ward Ald. Debra Silverstein renewed her claim that Johnson went around her committee, where the video gambling ordinance was approved and a proposed repeal "belongs," in favor of a committee chaired by a mayoral ally.</p>
